article_lead.description: Markov-chain states distinguished by whether the process can leave them forever, a key to their long-run behaviour

new_bank_questions.title: A return without staying put
new_bank_questions.body: A two-state chain has P(A→A)=0.7, P(A→B)=0.3, P(B→A)=0.4 and P(B→B)=0.6. Is A recurrent even though it may leave immediately? Find its expected first return time from A.
new_bank_questions.answer: The finite chain is irreducible, so both states are positive recurrent. From B the geometric waiting time to hit A has mean 1/0.4=2.5. Starting A, return time is 1 with probability 0.7; otherwise it is 1 plus that waiting time. Its mean is 0.7(1)+0.3(1+2.5)=1.75. Leaving immediately does not prevent eventual return.
